macros

A macro is an ordinary Mix program (.mix) that you run from an app's Macros icon or Help menu. It can use the usual Mix facilities, including application commands and Bus verbs. Listing macros never executes them. Macros run with your normal session authority.

Folders and precedence

Every app scans four tiers, from lowest to highest precedence:

TierFolderScope
Built-in global/opt/mixos/share/macros/Every app
Built-in per-app/opt/mixos/share/macros/<app>/One app
User global~/.config/mixos/macros/Every app
User per-app~/.config/mixos/macros/<app>/One app

<app> is the component name, for example ced, dopus or term. An absolute MIXOS_SHARE replaces /opt/mixos/share. An absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME replaces ~/.config; otherwise the configuration root is $HOME/.config. Resolution needs an absolute HOME and does not create folders until you request a write or open a user folder.

A macro's id is its file stem: hello.mix has id hello. Ids contain only lowercase ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Dotfiles, directories and other extensions are excluded. .mx documents, invalid ids and symlinks that escape a root are reported as diagnostics. A scan is shallow; it does not traverse another app's folder.

For the same id, user per-app > user global > built-in per-app > built-in global. The catalogue lists the winning entries by id, labels each tier and marks entries that shadow lower tiers. Missing folders are fine.

Using the menu

The Macros icon is the first standard icon, immediately before search when the app provides search. It opens a transient drop-down directly beneath the icon. New macro… and Open Workshop come first, followed by this app's macros, then global macros, in catalogue order within each group. A dim dot marks built-ins. At most fifteen macros are shown; More in Workshop… reaches the rest. Workshop is planned; both Workshop entries currently open this app's user macro folder in Dopus, with xdg-open as the fallback.

The drop-down shares the menu bar's row sizes, font, padding and frame, with the same minimum width. Near the window's right edge it aligns to the icon's right edge. Oversized content scrolls inside the window. An empty catalogue shows No macros yet. The New macro title field uses the same measured width and anchored placement as the drop-down, with a full text-field height. Creation errors wrap below the field within that frame. Tall menus stay below the title-bar icon and scroll vertically, preserving access to the icon. Horizontal scrolling is used only for rows wider than the available content area.

Left release runs a macro; right release edits it. Arrows move the highlight, Enter runs, Shift+Enter edits, and a letter jumps to the next matching title. Run, edit, Escape and an outside click close the menu and release its keys. One macro runs per window. A busy dot appears on the icon, and the first menu entry becomes Stop "Title". Stop kills the process group and reaps the child in the background. Closing the menu leaves the run alone; closing the app requests termination and background reaping.

Macro rows are dimmed while a macro runs. Ctrl+Enter in the editor still saves, and reports that a macro is already running in its output strip.

New macro… asks only for a title in a one-line field at the menu anchor. Enter creates the template in this app's user folder and opens the small editor; Escape cancels. If creation fails, the field keeps the title and shows the error inline so you can retry. Titles become ASCII slugs: Tidy imports creates tidy-imports.mix, then tidy-imports-2.mix on a clash. A title without ASCII letters or digits uses macro. Creation and copying never overwrite files. Editing a built-in first copies it to the matching user tier.

The small editor is a non-modal floating window using the shared editor. Click its text to edit; the app remains usable alongside it. Ctrl+S saves and refreshes the menu catalogue. Ctrl+Enter saves then runs. Open in Ced hands off larger edits, with xdg-open as fallback. Discovery, file storage, launchers and notification work run on background threads.

Failed creates keep the title field and show the destination path and OS reason inline. Failed built-in copies show the same kind of error in the menu, without opening an editor. Editing reads an existing file and checks its atomic-save directory first. If permissions change while editing, save errors name the file and OS reason, and the edits remain available. The check and save share target resolution: a symlink's target directory is checked, rather than the directory holding the link. Read-only macro files are refused inline, including in writable directories.

Saving keeps the document visible and editable, even during discovery. Closing a dirty editor saves before closing; a failed save keeps the text and error visible. Outside clicks dismiss menus with the same click-through behaviour as the toolkit menu bar. Catalogue changes close an open macro list so a stale highlight cannot select a different file.

Every completed run posts a notifyd toast: title and done or failed status, plus the last few output lines. Show output opens that run's retained output in the editor's bottom strip. The runner retains the last 64 KiB of combined standard output and standard error. If notifyd is absent or sending fails, the output strip opens automatically. A successful run without output still reports done.

One lazy native Bus client per process registers a distinct <app>-macros-<pid> service and subscribes to notify.changed before posting. There are no notification subprocesses or outcome polls. Deliveries request a repaint of the originating viewport. Each window retains at most eight notification outputs, for up to five minutes; answering, dismissing, closing, expiry or closing the window releases them. A Bus failure after a successful send drops that notification's retained output without opening the editor. Each viewport has its own menu, editor and runner state. Closing its window also withdraws outstanding notifications with notify.close and stops its runner; the background manager kills the process group before reaping the leader. While another run is live, the output strip shows that run; an older notification's output can be viewed when idle.

Execution context

The runner starts /opt/mixos/bin/mix <path> directly, without a shell wrapper. An absolute MIXOS_MIX selects another Mix binary. Its working directory is your home, and it receives:

VariableValue
MIXOS_MACRO_APPApp component name
MIXOS_MACRO_IDMacro file stem
MIXOS_MACRO_TIERbuiltin-global, builtin-app, user-global or user-app
MIXOS_MACRO_PATHFull macro path

For example, save this as ~/.config/mixos/macros/hello.mix:

-- title: Hello desktop
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0

print("Hello from " .. env("MIXOS_MACRO_APP"))

The first -- title: in the leading comment header supplies the displayed title; otherwise the id is shown. Header reads are bounded to 8 KiB.

Library boundaries

libs/macros is a core library with no egui dependency. It resolves roots, discovers files, creates or copies user macros and owns the background runner. toolkit::menu::anchored reuses menu navigation and row rendering. toolkit::macros::State joins the menu and shared editor to the core, with toggle, reload and show methods. Its per-window adapter keeps runtime resources in the egui context while each app keeps the menu's open flag in its UI state. This keeps application engines below the GUI boundary in the application layering gate.

Bus verbs

Email, BusViewer, Monitor, Prefs, Screenshot, Ced, Dopus and Term serve the same macro surface under their component prefix. list, status and output are read-only. run, stop, reload and new have the same authority as executing an app command; running a macro executes user code.

Suffix after <app>.macros.BodyReply
list{}{macros:[{id,title,tier,path,shadows}], diagnostics:[{path,message}], scanned:true}
reload{}Rescan and return the list shape
run{id}{accepted:true, run, id, title}; NOT_FOUND for unknown ids, BUSY while running
status{}{state,run,id,title,origin,started,exit,error}
output{}{run,text,dropped}; the retained 64 KiB tail
stop{}{stopping:bool}; termination is asynchronous
new{title}UNAVAILABLE until title-based creation lands

Refusals use rc 10 and {error_code,message}. Bodies are limited to 8192 bytes before JSON parsing.

Error codeMeaning
INVALID_ARGUMENTBad or oversized body, unknown fields, missing or empty id/title
NOT_FOUNDUnknown macro id
BUSYA macro is already running
UNAVAILABLEnew is not yet available, or no absolute HOME/roots
INTERNALScan error, worker failure or dropped reply channel

The first list and every reload scan off the caller's thread and defer the reply. Run loads the catalogue first if necessary and answers acceptance, not completion. Run numbers increase only for accepted runs within the app process. A manager-thread start refusal preserves the previous number and identity and emits no finished event. A child spawn failure after acceptance emits one failed_to_start event. States are idle, running, exited, failed and failed_to_start; a signal gives exit:null. Idle identity fields are null. Origins are gui or bus.

Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished before starting a run. Once the manager has cleaned up and reaped the process, one event is queued with {run,id,title,origin,state,exit,error,dropped}. dropped is the output-tail flag; event_dropped counts lost Bus events. Delivery is bounded and best effort, like command execution events. Read status and output after a gap or reconnect. Completion uses a callback, without a polling loop.

Filesystem watching and per-app context adapters remain future work.
